text: Focus component: model_design. Use Tier 2 representation and component modification: replace both depthwise temporal convolutions in every NextItNetBlock with full channel-mixing causal dilated convolutions. The latest model achieved validation HR@10 of 0.605, below the recorded best of 0.625, so its separable temporal representation warrants a controlled architectural experiment. Depthwise convolutions filter each channel independently before pointwise mixing, which constrains how different item features interact across temporal offsets. Dense temporal kernels can learn those cross-channel, cross-offset relationships directly, potentially improving representations of movie purchase transitions. Preserve the existing sigmoid gate, pointwise projections, normalization, residual connections, padding masks, and dilation pattern so that temporal convolution connectivity is the single experimental change. Keep all eight constants, embedding initialization, constructor and scoring interfaces, and frozen host behavior unchanged. Maintain left-only convolution padding to ensure every sequence representation remains causal. Evaluate this candidate through the host using validation HR@10, comparing it with both 0.605 and the best available checkpoint; any improvement would support the hypothesis that separable temporal filtering is limiting performance. This uses one candidate slot and retains a single NextItNet, with additional computation confined to its convolutional blocks.
